column1: # Permissions the provider may list for a stranger from a corpus file that passes the default lint run
# (exit 0).  One line per entry, tab separated: class, name regex, actions regex, files, reason.  The
# regexes match the whole name and the whole actions string.  ${user.home} and ${java.io.tmpdir} in a name
# regex stand for the property value, quoted.
# files: the corpus files (paths relative to the corpus directory, ; separated; * in a name stands for any
# characters but a slash) that may grant it.  An entry covers only those files: another file that is listed
# the same permission fails the test, and so does a name no file grants (a stale reference).
# reason: its own sentence, at least 25 characters, different from every other entry, and citing a fixture
# the entry names.  Every entry must also be matched by a listed permission (no dead entries) and none may
# rate HIGH in the catalogue.  A listed permission that is neither here nor implies one of the cross-check

column5: SerialObjectPermission for the one class net.jini.io.MarshalledInstance: it names a single class with no wildcard, so it opens no further class to deserialisation for a stranger (n42-serialobject-named-clean).
Read-only below the fixed directory /opt/app/conf, or its drive-letter form: no write and no root or home wildcard, so a stranger reads only the files under that one directory (ok2-fileread-dir).
Read-only below the fixed directory data/app on any drive letter: the narrow fixed path keeps it outside the drive-root and home rules, and it carries no write (ok2-fileread-dir).

Write only below the hidden application directory .myapp in the user home, so a stranger can change the application own files and nothing else in the home; clean in both runs (n23-home-subdir-write-clean).

Write below the relative directory lib: where that is depends on the working directory of whoever starts the service, which the lint rules clean in both runs; a stranger could write to that tree (f14-rel-sub-write).
The name is a property expansion that yields Oracle Corporation, a string that is no RuntimePermission name of the platform, so the grant implies nothing a check ever asks for (v09-name-prop).
define* is not a BasicPermission wildcard (only * and .* are), so it matches the single name define*, which no check ever asks for; clean in both runs (r21-rt-defineS).
The name is the literal text setu0053ecurityManager, not a unicode escape for setSecurityManager, so it implies only that name; clean in both runs (v02-unicode-name).
The name contains a line break, so it is not setSecurityManager and implies only that literal string, which no check asks for; clean in both runs (v04-continuation).
shutdownHooks lets a stranger register a hook that runs at VM exit and can delay it; the catalogue rates it clean, which the lint accepts in both runs (r15-rt-shutdownHooks).

authProvider.* is a BasicPermission wildcard for the names authProvider.X (obtaining a named authentication provider); the catalogue rates it clean, which the lint accepts in both runs (c12-sec-authProvider_S).
getProperty.* is a BasicPermission wildcard for reading any Security property by name; the catalogue rates it clean, which the lint accepts in both runs (c04-sec-getProperty_S).
set* is not a BasicPermission wildcard (only * and .* are), so it implies only the literal name set*, which no check asks for; clean in both runs (c16-sec-setS).
getDomainCombiner lets a stranger read the domain combiner of an access-control context; the catalogue rates it clean, which the lint accepts in both runs (c14-sec-getDomainCombiner).
AssertPrincipalPermission for one exact X500Principal, CN=gateway,O=Example: a stranger may assert only that identity, no wildcard principal; clean in both runs (n47-assertprincipal-exact-clean).
GrantPermission ceiling of localhost listen and accept on ports 1024 and up: it limits what may be granted onward to unprivileged local ports; clean in both runs (n34-grantperm-narrow-clean).

readlink on every file lets a stranger learn where any symbolic link points, but neither read nor change the target; the catalogue rates it D5 (MEDIUM) so the default run exits 0 (f05-allfiles-readlink).

Read of everything below a drive root: a stranger may read any file on the drive that the process can read, keys and configuration included; accepted only because the catalogue rates a root read D5, not D1 (f18-cdrive-dash-read).

Read of the whole user-home tree: a stranger may read every file under the home directory, credentials and keystores stored there included; accepted only as the catalogue rates it D5 (n26-home-read-medium).
Write to the files directly inside the temp directory, not below it: a stranger can plant or overwrite temp files but cannot create subdirectories; D5 in the catalogue (n20-tmpdir-star-write).

SerializablePermission enableSubstitution lets code substitute objects while serialising or deserialising, so a stranger could swap in an object of its choice; D5 in the catalogue (j08-serial-subclass).
accessClassInPackage.sun.* opens every sun.* internal package to a stranger, including the unsupported APIs; the catalogue rates it D5 and not HIGH (r07-rt-accessClassInPackage_sun_S).
accessClassInPackage.sun.misc opens the sun.misc package to a stranger, the home of Unsafe where the platform provides it; the catalogue rates it D5 (r06-rt-accessClassInPackage_sun_misc).
accessDeclaredMembers lets a stranger reflect on the private members of any class it can see, breaking the encapsulation of those classes; D5 in the catalogue (r05-rt-accessDeclaredMembers).
charsetProvider lets a stranger register a character-set provider and so change how bytes are decoded in the whole VM; D5 in the catalogue (r22-rt-charsetProvider).

enableContextClassLoaderOverride lets a stranger subclass Thread and override the context class loader accessors, steering which loader library code uses; D5 (r23-rt-enableContextClassLoaderOverride).
exitVM lets a stranger stop the whole VM at any exit status: a denial of service, not a disclosure or code execution; D5 in the catalogue (r16-rt-exitVM).
exitVM.0 lets a stranger end the VM with exit status 0 only, which a supervisor may read as a normal shutdown; D5 in the catalogue (r17-rt-exitVM_0).
getClassLoader returns the class loader of any class to a stranger, from which loader-held classes and resources can be reached; D5 in the catalogue (r04-rt-getClassLoader).
manageProcess lets a stranger inspect and end operating-system processes through ProcessHandle, which includes processes other than this VM; D5 in the catalogue (r24-rt-manageProcess).
modifyThread lets a stranger interrupt, suspend or reprioritise any thread of the VM, a denial of service against the service threads; D5 in the catalogue (r12-rt-modifyThread).
modifyThreadGroup lets a stranger change the groups and threads below any thread group, including the service groups; D5 in the catalogue (r13-rt-modifyThreadGroup).
readFileDescriptor lets a stranger read from an already open file descriptor, bypassing the path-based FilePermission checks; D5 in the catalogue (r19-rt-readFileDescriptor).
setContextClassLoader lets a stranger replace the context class loader of a thread, redirecting service loading done on that thread; D5 in the catalogue (r03-rt-setContextClassLoader).
setIO lets a stranger replace System.in, System.out and System.err for the whole VM, capturing or redirecting all console traffic; accepted only as the catalogue rates it D5 (r14-rt-setIO).
writeFileDescriptor lets a stranger write to an already open file descriptor, bypassing the path-based FilePermission checks; D5 in the catalogue (r18-rt-writeFileDescriptor).
newProxyInPackage.* lets a stranger define dynamic proxies for interfaces in any package, including non-public ones; D5 in the catalogue (x03-reflect-proxy).
SocketPermission * with resolve only: a stranger may look up any host name, which can leak data through DNS, but may not connect or listen; D5 in the catalogue (s03-socket-resolve).
SocketPermission *.com connect: a stranger may open connections to any .com host and so send data out to it; accepted only as the catalogue rates it D5 (s04-socket-subnet).
createPolicy.JavaPolicy lets a stranger construct a Policy object of the default type, but not install it; D5 in the catalogue (c03-sec-createPolicy_JavaPolicy).
getPolicy lets a stranger read the installed Policy and so learn what is granted to whom; D5 in the catalogue (c01-sec-getPolicy).
SQLPermission setNetworkTimeout lets a stranger change the network timeout of JDBC connections, which can stall or cut them; D5 in the catalogue (n89-sql-setnetworktimeout-unscoped).
createLoginContext.* lets a stranger create a LoginContext for any configuration entry and so start a login through it; D5 in the catalogue (u01-auth-createLoginContext_S).
doAs lets a stranger run an action as any Subject it can obtain; accepted only as the catalogue rates it D5, though it is an identity operation (u02-auth-doAs).
getLoginConfiguration lets a stranger read the JAAS login configuration and so learn which login modules and options protect the service; D5 (u10-auth-getLoginConfiguration).
getSubject lets a stranger read the Subject of the current access-control context and so see its principals and public credentials; D5 in the catalogue (u05-auth-getSubject).
modifyPublicCredentials lets a stranger add or remove public credentials of a Subject, which can plant a credential the service later trusts; accepted only as D5 (u07-auth-modifyPublicCredentials).
refreshLoginConfiguration lets a stranger make the JVM reload the login configuration, which is harmful only after the file was changed; D5 (u11-auth-refreshLoginConfiguration).
setLoginConfiguration lets a stranger replace the JVM-wide JAAS configuration and so choose the login modules that authenticate everyone; accepted only as D5 (u06-auth-setLoginConfiguration).
